_comment: Every claim the site makes about itself and the programme, with its status. docs/reality.md and the status tables on the pages are generated from this file by admin/build/gen_reality.py. shipped means it exists in the repository, runs, and has been exercised, at the version shown; proposed means the brief or the memo says how and it is not built; absent means it is deliberately not here. If it is not listed here, it does not exist, whatever the brief says.

statuses.shipped: exists in the repository, runs, and was exercised at the version shown
statuses.proposed: the brief or the memo says how; not built; described only in the future tense
statuses.absent: deliberately not on this site; comes as a later version, lives elsewhere, or never

features.title: One version in admin/build/version.txt, a release history, and four CI jobs: validate, tag, deploy, verify live
features.notes: Copied from secrets.sgit.ai, the newest gate in the estate. A clean push is not a release: verify-live polls the host.

features.title: The RiskMandate chrome (head, header, breadcrumbs, footer, CSP) generated into every page from one definition
features.notes: The look of riskmandate.ai; every colour is a token in one file.

features.title: Six themes picked from the header and kept in the reader's browser: RiskMandate (the default), Canvas, Night, Ember, Paper, Blueprint
features.notes: The newsroom's five themes mapped onto this site's tokens, plus riskmandate.ai's own dark. Every colour is a token in one file; the gate checks every theme for every token and for contrast.

features.title: A markdown twin for every page, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and sitemap.xml, generated from the pages
features.notes: Links inside the markdown point at markdown.

features.title: The eight-check gate: version agreement, links and orphans, canonical host, the leak tripwire, no foreign runtime origin, the data holding together, reality regenerating identically, the house words
features.notes: The house words are riskmandate.ai's rules, listed on the admin page and in WORD_RULES in admin/build/validate.js. The verbatim brief and memo are exempt.

features.title: The review folder: the brief read as intent, each node anchored to a section of the brief, validated and rendered
features.notes: The top-down half only; see site.review-derived.

features.title: The derived half of the review folder: the code graph from parsers, the join with a coverage figure, every commit read upwards, the navigator as web components
features.notes: The review brief asks for it from the first commit; this site has the intent half and says so in review/BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md.

features.title: The brief and the memo published in full, never edited, with the corrections file beside them
features.notes: The newsroom article of 20 October 2026 and the voice memo of the same day, byte for byte, with its digest.

features.title: A start-here page: what a customer does first, in order, with the links to do it
features.notes: The brief's first fix for pages that were hard to understand; each customer will show where it still is.

features.title: A page per customer with the fields the brief asks to track, generated from data/customers.json, with no contact details
features.notes: Start date, first behaviour policy with rows and gaps, steps done, credit used, topped up, and the follow-up log. One worked example, marked as such.

features.title: Seven milestone steps shared across the batch, from in-with-credit to the usage moment
features.notes: The objectives per customer are theirs; the steps are the shared shape so the batch reads in one table.

features.title: The daily follow-up: three questions, recorded on the customer page as a log
features.notes: What they did, what got in the way, what is next. Daily if that is what helps; the record is the summary.

features.title: The three questions the programme exists to answer, with a findings table that starts empty
features.notes: The simplest useful behaviour policy, the entry point with least friction, the price that feels fair.

features.title: Every reader starts with £50 of credit, and every page has a price by its kind, metered by SG Meter from api.newsroom.sgit.ai
features.notes: Meter v1.4.1 from the API release v0.2.5, pinned and checked against its hash. Charged by how far down a page is read; nothing is blocked. The balance lives in the reader's browser.

features.title: A payment link, so a top-up moves money
features.notes: Until the lead adds one, the top-up page is the meter's simulated cart, which says so.

features.title: Six behaviour policies to install in minutes: four for Claude Code with a line and a tested hook, two for ChatGPT and Claude with a line; a starter pack for the four
features.notes: Built from riskmandate.ai's rules, copied byte for byte. Every hook refusal in the tests has an allowed twin.

features.title: Three storyboards drawn in the reader's browser by the kit from api.storyboards.sgit.ai: what an ABP is, your first policy, the first batch
features.notes: The kit is pinned and loaded with its integrity strings; its delay attributes are allowed by hash and no other inline style.

features.title: Animated demos of a session: installing and trying a policy in Claude Code, and the send-as-you line in ChatGPT
features.notes: Illustrations of what each policy's page promises, labelled as such; not recordings. Still and complete with reduced motion or no JavaScript.

features.title: A form on this site for the next batch, encrypted in the browser to the riskmandate.ai agent's lane
features.notes: Today the route is the riskmandate.ai contact form or an email to agent@riskmandate.ai; the page says so.

features.title: The private record per customer (contact details, the agreed objectives in full, the private notes) in a vault the lead holds
features.notes: Never in this repository. The public page carries the summary.

features.title: A behaviour policy for each of the agents the lead runs, produced by the agent that is wired in
features.notes: The memo of 20 October: about ten agents; two have one today, on riskmandate.ai/team/.

features.title: This site's row on the honest column at nfrs.sgit.ai
features.notes: Another repository; the ask is recorded.

features.title: Accounts, sign-in or a customer login on this site
features.notes: The site is static. The meter, when wired, carries its own reading account, as on the newsroom.

features.title: Customer contact details, company names that are not already public, or private notes in this repository
features.notes: The gate fails on anything contact-shaped in data/customers.json.

features.title: A score, rating or level on any behaviour policy
features.notes: An Agent Behaviour Policy describes and does not judge. The gate fails on the words.
